name: Triglav National Park
blurb: Limestone Julian Alps: chamois, marmots and the wolf and eagle above them.

tip.title: Remove the wolf
tip.text: Take the wolf out and watch deer and chamois numbers and the carcasses that ravens, foxes and eagles live on.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: Light is short in deep valleys and in winter, so sun-warmed slopes and early snow-free ground matter for plant growth.
A widespread forest tree in the park; its nuts are eaten by squirrels and dormice, and roe deer browse it.
Fescue and other grasses of the alpine pastures; ibex eat mostly grass, and chamois and marmots graze meadow grasses in summer.
A mat-forming alpine plant of limestone outcrops and gravel where snow melts early.
Grazes alpine meadows in summer and moves down into forest in winter, eating conifers and bark.
Eats mostly grass, adding herbs in summer and dwarf shrubs in winter. Reintroduced to Slovenia in the 1890s.
A small forest deer, often recorded in the park, that browses trees such as beech.
A large deer of the valleys and forests, and a main prey of the wolf.
Colonial burrower of alpine meadows that eats grasses, herbs and insects and hibernates for much of the year.
A tree-dwelling seed eater that feeds on beech nuts and other forest seeds.
A generalist hunter and scavenger, recorded eating marmots, squirrels, dormice and deer.
A forest and village-edge predator that hunts dormice and squirrels.
A scavenging crow that feeds on the carcasses of deer and chamois.
Pack hunter of deer and chamois, returning to the Alps; its kills feed scavengers.
Hunts alpine pastures above the tree line, taking marmots and young ibex, and scavenges carcasses.
